# BAD-096 — Expression index on lower(btrim(scene_title)) for the two acquisition tables

## Brief
BAD-095 adds an unwindowed min(created_at) grouped by lower(btrim(scene_title)) over private.scene_imports and private.scene_saves, to power the admin /scenes First imported column. It is the only query on that page that scans whole tables rather than a window, and it cannot be narrowed: sorting by First imported must order every scene before the page's 50 rows are taken. No existing index covers the key expression, so the plan is two sequential scans into a HashAggregate. Affordable now and deliberately left alone in BAD-095 (a migration is out of that ticket's scope and deploys from CI), but it is the first thing on this page that gets slower while the window stays the same width.

Evidence: Indexes present: scene_imports_created_at_idx (created_at desc) and scene_imports_lower_created_at_idx (lower(email), created_at desc) from migrations 0010; scene_saves has (lower(email), created_at desc) 0003, a bucket index 0006 and (created_at desc) 0011. None is on the title expression. Measured with explain (analyze, buffers) against the local stack (653 scene_imports, 2639 scene_saves): HashAggregate, two Seq Scans, 56 shared buffer hits, 1.076 ms. That is ~0.3 us/row, so a million acquisition rows is a few hundred ms on one of the three connections admin/src/lib/db.ts pools — under Cloud Run's 300s ceiling but the point where the index earns its keep. admin/CLAUDE.md records a real 504 on 2026-08-20 from unindexed whole-table scans on this dashboard.
